Report: Ferrari were SO impressed by the Xiaomi SU7, they bought one
Jo Borrás
| Jul 29 2025 - 6:47 pm PT
18 Comments
With its
tire-blistering acceleration
and
record-setting performance
, the Xiaomi SU7 Ultra has been getting attention throughout the auto industry, impressing everyone who’s seen it. That “everyone” now seems to include the OG supercar brand, itself.
CarNewsChina
posted pictures from a Weibo user that reportedly show a Xiaomi SU7 Ultra exiting the storied Ferrari factory in Maranello, Italy. According to a Chinese blogger going by 西米露在博洛尼亚 (which seems to translate to “Sago Dessert in Bologna”), the prancing horse brand is actively benchmarking the Chinese hypercar for its own upcoming EV.
The SU7 Ultra was definitely coming from inside Ferrari’s facility. After verification, we learned this specific vehicle was officially purchased by Ferrari for testing, and the development of their next-generation electric platform.
西米露在博洛尼亚
Yet another Chinese auto blogger,
苏黎世贝勒爷
, claims that Ferrari representatives visited Xiaomi headquarters last year,
allegedly to discuss the joint development of next-generation high-performance EV motors
.
The Xiaomi SU7 Ultra made its debut last year
, promising 1,548 hp, sub 2.0-second 0-60 mph times, and a top speed well over 200 mph – all at a price lower than a Tesla Model S Plaid or
Porsche Taycan Turbo GT
. The car sold out almost immediately after it was unveiled, racking up some 50,000 orders almost overnight.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
The new electric benchmark
Xiaomi SU7 Ultra at Fiorano; via Weibo user Piniluoshan.
In the automotive world, “
benchmarking
” is a process in which car companies systematically tear down each others’ competitive products to compare everything from sound insulation, vehicle ride and handling, component materials, and even manufacturing methods against their own or against other industry leaders. The goal is to evaluate performance, cost, quality, and other key metrics, effectively figuring out “where they stand” in the market.
If Ferrari really
did
buy an SU7 to benchmark it against their own upcoming electric supercar, it’s more than just a curiosity –
it could mean that the highest tiers of automotive innovation have shifted from West to East
. Maybe forever.
Featured image via Xiaomi; sources throughout the post.

data.title: Show HN: I built an AI that turns any book into a text adventure game
data.author: rcrKnight
data.article_summary: KathaaVerse是一个互动文本 fiction 平台，用户可以将书籍转化为互动冒险体验。平台提供多种类型的故事，包括奇幻与魔法、科幻、当代小说以及反乌托邦与惊悚类别。经典作品如《爱丽丝梦游仙境》、《哈利波特与魔法石》、《魔戒》、《沙丘》和《1984》等都被收录其中，用户可以根据自己喜好选择并引导情节发展。每个故事都提供“开始”选项，让用户沉浸于不同的虚构世界中，体验个性化的冒险旅程。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI生成叙事文本的质量、用户与AI在叙事中的互动、技术实现的挑战与建议、以及AI生成内容的价值问题。

不同观点：
• **AI在生成逻辑叙事方面的不足**：[why_at] 提到AI在生成像《霍比特人》这样的故事时，出现了重复角色和缺乏逻辑性的问题，表明AI在保持连贯叙事方面的不足。

• **用户主导叙事与AI被动回应的矛盾**：[kmnc] 认为AI往往只是被动回应，用户主导了叙事方向，导致故事变得可预测、浅薄且重复，质疑这种模式下的创意性。

• **AI生成内容的情感缺失**：[jaysonelliot] 指出AI生成的内容缺乏人类作者的情感和深度，认为即使在不知道内容由AI生成的情况下，仍能感受到内容的空虚和不满足，尤其是与人类创作的文本冒险游戏相比。

• **技术优化建议**：[spdustin] 提供了关于如何通过结构化选择和引导AI生成更具互动性和连贯性的故事的技术建议，强调了通过指令和随机性（RNG）的结合来改善叙事体验。

• **对AI生成故事的趣味性认可**：[fifticon] 和 [oooyay] 等用户对AI生成故事的趣味性和潜力表示认可，尽管他们遇到了技术问题，如速率限制，但仍对整体体验持积极态度。

• **AI生成内容的价值质疑**：[HellDunkel] 从艺术交流的角度质疑AI生成内容的价值，认为AI生成内容缺乏与人类沟通的深度和意义。

补充讨论：
• **技术实现中的问题**：[bArray]、[mNovak] 和 [superkacper4] 提到了在实际使用中遇到的技术问题，如速率限制错误、故事显示不全、以及黑暗模式崩溃等。

• **多选择题模式的建议**：[sjw987] 提出了一种基于现有书籍内容生成多选择题的替代方案，认为这样可以避免AI生成故事时偏离原著，同时也能用于学习和研究。

• **经典文学作品的潜在应用**：[abrookewood] 和 [BaudouinVH] 讨论了AI生成内容在经典文学作品中的潜在应用，如《卡夫卡的审判》或《城堡》，提出了对预计算路径和存储结果的建议以优化体验。

争议焦点：
• **AI生成内容的创意性与被动性之间的平衡**：用户对于AI在叙事中应扮演的角色存在分歧，一部分用户希望AI能更主动引导故事，另一部分用户则认为AI只是被动响应，缺乏创意性。
• **AI生成内容的价值和意义**：部分用户质疑AI生成内容是否具有与人类创作内容相同的艺术和交流价值，这一问题在讨论中引发了对AI生成内容未来发展的深思。

44725202.article_summary: KathaaVerse是一个互动文本 fiction 平台，用户可以将书籍转化为互动冒险体验。平台提供多种类型的故事，包括奇幻与魔法、科幻、当代小说以及反乌托邦与惊悚类别。经典作品如《爱丽丝梦游仙境》、《哈利波特与魔法石》、《魔戒》、《沙丘》和《1984》等都被收录其中，用户可以根据自己喜好选择并引导情节发展。每个故事都提供“开始”选项，让用户沉浸于不同的虚构世界中，体验个性化的冒险旅程。
44725202.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI生成叙事文本的质量、用户与AI在叙事中的互动、技术实现的挑战与建议、以及AI生成内容的价值问题。

不同观点：
• **AI在生成逻辑叙事方面的不足**：[why_at] 提到AI在生成像《霍比特人》这样的故事时，出现了重复角色和缺乏逻辑性的问题，表明AI在保持连贯叙事方面的不足。

• **用户主导叙事与AI被动回应的矛盾**：[kmnc] 认为AI往往只是被动回应，用户主导了叙事方向，导致故事变得可预测、浅薄且重复，质疑这种模式下的创意性。

• **AI生成内容的情感缺失**：[jaysonelliot] 指出AI生成的内容缺乏人类作者的情感和深度，认为即使在不知道内容由AI生成的情况下，仍能感受到内容的空虚和不满足，尤其是与人类创作的文本冒险游戏相比。

• **技术优化建议**：[spdustin] 提供了关于如何通过结构化选择和引导AI生成更具互动性和连贯性的故事的技术建议，强调了通过指令和随机性（RNG）的结合来改善叙事体验。

• **对AI生成故事的趣味性认可**：[fifticon] 和 [oooyay] 等用户对AI生成故事的趣味性和潜力表示认可，尽管他们遇到了技术问题，如速率限制，但仍对整体体验持积极态度。

• **AI生成内容的价值质疑**：[HellDunkel] 从艺术交流的角度质疑AI生成内容的价值，认为AI生成内容缺乏与人类沟通的深度和意义。

补充讨论：
• **技术实现中的问题**：[bArray]、[mNovak] 和 [superkacper4] 提到了在实际使用中遇到的技术问题，如速率限制错误、故事显示不全、以及黑暗模式崩溃等。

• **多选择题模式的建议**：[sjw987] 提出了一种基于现有书籍内容生成多选择题的替代方案，认为这样可以避免AI生成故事时偏离原著，同时也能用于学习和研究。

• **经典文学作品的潜在应用**：[abrookewood] 和 [BaudouinVH] 讨论了AI生成内容在经典文学作品中的潜在应用，如《卡夫卡的审判》或《城堡》，提出了对预计算路径和存储结果的建议以优化体验。

争议焦点：
• **AI生成内容的创意性与被动性之间的平衡**：用户对于AI在叙事中应扮演的角色存在分歧，一部分用户希望AI能更主动引导故事，另一部分用户则认为AI只是被动响应，缺乏创意性。
• **AI生成内容的价值和意义**：部分用户质疑AI生成内容是否具有与人类创作内容相同的艺术和交流价值，这一问题在讨论中引发了对AI生成内容未来发展的深思。

data.title: Silicon Is Coming to Smartphone Batteries for a Big Energy Boost
data.author: defrost
data.article_summary: Enovix公司开发了一种采用硅负极的新型电池AI-1，其能量密度比当前主流智能手机电池高出约20%。这一突破有望大幅提升智能手机的电池续航能力。硅材料的应用使得电池可以在相同体积下储存更多能量，为消费电子产品带来显著的性能提升。这一技术进步对于智能手机及其他便携设备具有重要意义。文章由IEEE Spectrum的撰稿编辑Charles Q. Choi撰写。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Apple Vision Pro电池技术的未来发展及其市场潜力

不同观点：
• kridsdale3认为，通过改进电池技术，未来的Apple Vision Pro电池包可以缩小至现有尺寸的1/3（可能不需要使用腰包），或者在现有功耗水平下续航时间延长3倍。他还提到，传闻下一代Vision Pro将采用M4级别的芯片，进一步降低功耗。因此，kridsdale3预测，经过1到2次迭代，Apple可能会推出一款更具大众市场吸引力的产品。

• malchow则关注电池技术的具体材料改进，指出新电池技术使用100%活性硅材料作为阳极，而非仅在石墨中掺杂5%的硅。他还分享了一个展示生产过程的预览视频链接，对技术的先进性表示赞赏。

补充讨论：
• kridsdale3的观点更侧重于Apple Vision Pro整体产品的市场潜力和用户体验的改进，特别是重量、热量和续航时间等方面。
• malchow的观点则聚焦于电池技术本身的创新，特别是材料科学方面的突破，如100%活性硅材料在阳极中的应用。
• 争议的焦点可能在于技术的实际应用和市场化时间。kridsdale3更乐观地预计短期内可以看到改进产品，而malchow则关注技术的实际生产和实现。
• malchow提供的视频链接为讨论增添了技术细节和可视化信息，使讨论更加具体和生动。

总结来看，评论主要围绕Apple Vision Pro电池技术的未来发展，讨论了电池体积和续航时间的改进潜力，以及新材料和生产工艺的创新。同时，也对技术实现和市场化的前景存在一定乐观但有区别的预期。

data.title: YouTube will identify and restrict minors' accounts with AI
data.author: conor-
data.article_summary: YouTube将从下个月开始使用人工智能技术通过账户年龄和活动来识别美国未成年用户，并自动对其账户实施限制，如屏蔽年龄限制内容、减少个性化广告、推送休息提醒以及限制敏感话题的视频推荐。此外，上传视频或留言时会自动出现隐私提醒。若系统判断错误，用户可通过上传政府ID、自拍或输入信用卡验证年龄。此举是YouTube加强未成年人网络安全的一部分，并将在其他国家逐步推广。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：在HTTP协议中引入内容分级系统的可行性与影响

不同观点：
• [支持观点 - atonse]  
   支持在HTTP协议中引入内容分级系统，认为可以通过HTTP头部字段（如X-Minimum-Recommended-Age或X-Contains-Content-Themes）标示页面内容，例如是否包含暴力、裸体等。这种方法可以保护隐私，并允许父母通过浏览器设置控制孩子可以访问的内容。同时，提到YouTube已经要求创作者指定观众群体，认为这种方式可以更精细地控制内容访问，而不必完全屏蔽平台。

• [反对观点 - RamblingCTO]  
   认为这种内容分级系统有些“反乌托邦”色彩，尤其在YouTube已经因其内容审核问题备受批评的情况下。同时，RamblingCTO对YouTube的垄断地位表示不满，认为这种系统可能反而巩固YouTube的统治地位，而不是带来真正的改变。他表达了对去中心化平台（如Peertube）的期望，但认为这些替代平台目前还不够好。

补充讨论：
• [争议焦点]  
   争议的焦点在于内容分级系统的潜在效果。支持者认为它有助于更精细地控制内容访问，保护隐私，同时方便家长管理孩子浏览的内容。而反对者则担心这种系统可能被大平台利用，进一步巩固其垄断地位，并且对内容审核问题带来新的挑战。

• [技术实现的简单性与现实复杂性]  
   atonse认为技术上只需添加几个HTTP头部字段，实现简单，且已有类似做法（如YouTube的观众指定功能）。但RamblingCTO则隐含指出，内容分级涉及的不只是技术问题，还有更广泛的社会和政治影响，尤其是平台垄断和内容审核方面。

• [对替代平台的期望]  
   RamblingCTO提到去中心化平台（如Peertube），显示出对当前大平台的不满，并希望有更好的替代品。然而，他也承认这些替代平台目前还不够成熟。这引出了一个额外讨论点：如何在大平台垄断的现状下寻找和支持替代方案。

YouTube will identify and restrict minors’ accounts with AI
Next month, YouTube will use an account’s age and activity to determine if it belongs to someone under 18.
Next month, YouTube will use an account’s age and activity to determine if it belongs to someone under 18.
by
Emma Roth
Close

Link
Facebook
Threads
Image: Alex Castro / The Verge
Emma Roth
is a news writer who covers the streaming wars, consumer tech, crypto, social media, and much more. Previously, she was a writer and editor at MUO.
YouTube will soon begin using AI-powered age estimation technology to figure out which users are under the age of 18.
Starting August 13th
, YouTube will detect underage users in the US based on their activity and the age of their account, allowing the platform to automatically apply restrictions.
These accounts will get the same protections YouTube already offers to users who identify themselves as under 18, including a block on age-restricted videos, non-personalized ads,
“take a break” notifications
, and a
limit on repeated video recommendations
about sensitive topics, such as body image. The platform will also automatically turn on reminders about privacy when users upload a video or leave a comment.
Google first announced plans to use
machine learning to power age estimation
earlier this year, which aligns with a global crackdown on child safety online. Last week, the
UK’s online age verification rules
went into effect, requiring users to verify their ages on sites with porn or content deemed “harmful.” Several states have passed laws
blocking minors from accessing porn sites
, while efforts to age-gate social media platforms have largely
fallen flat
. The European Union is also testing
an age verification prototype
that it will eventually link with digital IDs.
Related
The UK is slogging through an online age-gate apocalypse
Reddit and Discord’s UK age verification can be defeated by Death Stranding’s photo mode
YouTube will notify users if it determines they are under 18, but if the platform gets it wrong, users can verify their age by uploading a government ID, taking a selfie, or entering a credit card. The platform notes that some creators may “experience a shift in their audience categorized as teens,” potentially resulting in less ad revenue, since minors aren’t shown personalized ads.
“Over the next few weeks, we’ll begin to roll out machine learning to a small set of users in the US to estimate their age, so that teens are treated as teens and adults as adults,” James Beser, YouTube’s director of product management,
writes in a post explaining the change
. Beser adds that YouTube will “closely monitor” the update before rolling it out to other countries.

data.title: My 2.5 year old laptop can write Space Invaders in JavaScript now (GLM-4.5 Air)
data.author: simonw
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了Simon Willison在2025年7月29日发布的一篇博客，讲述了在一台2.5年历史的笔记本电脑上使用GLM-4.5 Air模型和MLX库编写JavaScript版本的《太空入侵者》游戏。GLM-4.5模型由中国的Z.ai发布，具备较高的编码能力。尽管模型体积庞大（1060亿参数，205.78GB），但经过量化压缩，可以在64GB内存的MacBook Pro M2上运行。作者展示了如何配置和运行该模型，并成功生成了可运行的游戏代码。作者还提到，与两年前相比，本地运行的高质量编码模型性能显著提升，显示了2025年模型在个人设备上的快速发展。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）在本地硬件上运行的能力及其应用价值

不同观点：
• [NitpickLawyer] 认为，开源模型的质量和发布速度已经超越了他的预期。他从历史角度对比了GPT-J等早期模型与当前的GLM 4.5 Air、Mistral 3.2 Small等模型，指出这些新模型的能力显著提升，且在本地运行成为可能，这是两年前无法想象的。
• [bob1029] 强调现有硬件的能力被低估，批评了“ bitter lesson ”和“ efficient compute frontier ”等观点，认为这些理论可能误导了研究方向。他指出当前模型的效率低下，但通过降低权重精度仍能实现惊人的结果。
• [righthand] 对LLM的实际应用价值提出质疑，认为许多人使用LLM来增强演示文稿而非实现实际功能。他举例说明同事使用LLM生成复杂但无实际效用的解决方案。
• [alankarmisra] 认可LLM在本地运行的里程碑意义，但质疑其在特定领域（如Space Invaders）的实际价值，认为从GitHub等平台获取现有实现可能更有效。
• [lxgr] 提出一个科幻式的问题，探讨今日消费级硬件是否能运行未来的超级智能或代理，并引导讨论这种情景的可能性。
• [captainregex] 质疑本地AI的最大用户群体及其应用场景，认为当前使用本地AI更多是因为技术可行性而非实际需求。

补充讨论：
• [simonw] 和 [ddtaylor] 分享了实际测试结果，展示了新模型在本地运行的情况，并提供了相关链接和截图。
• [pulkitsh1234] 提出了对LLM运行硬件要求的疑问，希望有类似游戏“系统要求”的参考标准。
• [dust42] 对比了不同模型的表现，指出GLM-4.5 Air在某些任务上优于Claude Sonnet 4。
• [indigodaddy] 分享了使用LLM成功实现简单游戏的经历，并指出模型的某些不足之处。

争议焦点：
• LLM在本地硬件上的实际应用价值及其对未来研究和商业模式的影响是讨论的核心争议点。一方面，有人认为这是技术进步的里程碑，另一方面，有人质疑其实际效用和经济可行性。

44723316.article_content:
Simon Willison’s Weblog
Subscribe
My 2.5 year old laptop can write Space Invaders in JavaScript now, using GLM-4.5 Air and MLX
29th July 2025
I wrote about the new
GLM-4.5
model family yesterday—new open weight (MIT licensed) models from
Z.ai
in China which their benchmarks claim score highly in coding even against models such as Claude Sonnet 4.
The models are pretty big—the smaller GLM-4.5 Air model is still 106 billion total parameters, which
is 205.78GB
on Hugging Face.
Ivan Fioravanti
built
this
44GB 3bit quantized version for MLX
, specifically sized so people with 64GB machines could have a chance of running it. I tried it out... and it works
extremely well
.
I fed it the following prompt:
Write an HTML and JavaScript page implementing space invaders
And it churned away for a while and produced
the following
:
Clearly this isn’t a particularly novel example, but I still think it’s noteworthy that a model running on my 2.5 year old laptop (a 64GB MacBook Pro M2) is able to produce code like this—especially code that worked first time with no further edits needed.
How I ran the model
I had to run it using the current
main
branch of the
mlx-lm
library (to ensure I had
this commit
adding
glm4_moe
support). I ran that using
uv
like this:
uv run \
--with
'
https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-lm/archive/489e63376b963ac02b3b7223f778dbecc164716b.zip
'
\
python
Then in that Python interpreter I used the standard recipe for running MLX models:
from
mlx_lm
import
load
,
generate
model
,
tokenizer
=
load
(
"mlx-community/GLM-4.5-Air-3bit"
)
That downloaded 44GB of model weights to my
~/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--mlx-community--GLM-4.5-Air-3bit
folder.
Then:
prompt
=
"Write an HTML and JavaScript page implementing space invaders"
messages
=
[{
"role"
:
"user"
,
"content"
:
prompt
}]
prompt
=
tokenizer
.
apply_chat_template
(
messages
,
add_generation_prompt
=
True
)
response
=
generate
(
model
,
tokenizer
,
prompt
=
prompt
,
verbose
=
True
,
max_tokens
=
8192
)
The response started like this:
<think>
The user wants me to create a Space Invaders game using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. I need to create a complete, functional game with the following features:
Player spaceship that can move left/right and shoot
Enemy invaders that move in formation and shoot back
Score tracking
Lives/health system
Game over conditions [...]
Followed by the HTML and this debugging output:
Prompt: 14 tokens, 14.095 tokens-per-sec
Generation: 4193 tokens, 25.564 tokens-per-sec
Peak memory: 47.687 GB
You can see
the full transcript here
, or view
the source on GitHub
, or
try it out in your browser
.
A pelican for good measure
I ran
my pelican benchmark
against the full sized models
yesterday
, but I couldn’t resist trying it against this smaller 3bit model. Here’s what I got for
"Generate an SVG of a pelican riding a bicycle"
:
Here’s the
transcript for that
.
In both cases the model used around 48GB of RAM at peak, leaving me with just 16GB for everything else—I had to quit quite a few apps in order to get the model to run but the speed was pretty good once it got going.
Local coding models are really good now
It’s interesting how almost every model released in 2025 has specifically targeting coding. That focus has clearly been paying off: these coding models are getting
really good
now.
Two years ago when I
first tried LLaMA
I never
dreamed
that the same laptop I was using then would one day be able to run models with capabilities as strong as what I’m seeing from GLM 4.5 Air—and Mistral 3.2 Small, and Gemma 3, and Qwen 3, and a host of other high quality models that have emerged over the past six months.

data.title: The best available open weight LLMs now come from China
data.author: simonw
data.article_summary: 2025年7月，作者指出中国AI实验室推出的开源大语言模型在性能上超越了其他竞争对手，如Mistral、Gemma和Llama。作者详细列出了几款表现突出的模型，包括Moonshot的Kimi-K2-Instruct（1万亿参数）和Qwen的多款模型（2350亿至4800亿参数不等），以及Z.ai的GLM-4.5和GLM-4.5 Air（3550亿和1060亿参数）。这些模型大多提供了自己的API，并逐渐被其他供应商采用。作者还提到，自己能够在笔记本电脑上运行Qwen 30B和GLM-4.5 Air 106B模型。文章最后，作者猜测OpenAI可能因为想超越这些中国模型而延迟了其开源模型的发布。
data.comments_summary: 暂无评论

44736238.article_content:
Simon Willison’s Weblog
Subscribe
Something that has become undeniable this month is that the best available open weight models now come from the Chinese AI labs.
I continue to have a lot of love for Mistral, Gemma and Llama but my feeling is that Qwen, Moonshot and Z.ai have positively
smoked them
over the course of July.
Here's what came out this month, with links to my notes on each one:
Moonshot
Kimi-K2-Instruct
- 11th July, 1 trillion parameters
Qwen
Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507
- 21st July, 235 billion
Qwen
Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct
- 22nd July, 480 billion
Qwen
Qwen3-235B-A22B-Thinking-2507
- 25th July, 235 billion
Z.ai
GLM-4.5 and GLM-4.5 Air
- 28th July, 355 and 106 billion
Qwen
Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507
- 29th July, 30 billion
Qwen
Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507
- 30th July, 30 billion
Notably absent from this list is DeepSeek, but that's only because their last model release was
DeepSeek-R1-0528
back in April.
The only janky license among them is Kimi K2, which uses a non-OSI-compliant modified MIT. Qwen's models are all Apache 2 and Z.ai's are MIT.
The larger Chinese models all offer their own APIs and are increasingly available from other providers.  I've been able to run versions of the Qwen 30B and GLM-4.5 Air 106B models on my own laptop.
I can't help but wonder if part of the reason for the delay in release of OpenAI's open weights model comes from a desire to be notably better than this truly impressive lineup of Chinese models.

data.title: State of HTML 2025
data.author: xnx
data.article_summary: 2025年，第一届State of HTML调查由Lea Verou主导，吸引了21,000名参与者，创下新高。今年，Lea再次领导，新增35个功能，并引入图形与多媒体和性能两个新板块。该调查由Devographics组织，与贡献者、翻译者和志愿者合作，旨在衡量开发者对新HTML功能和浏览器API的认知，帮助跟踪其使用趋势。调查结果将影响浏览器厂商的路线图决策。任何从事网站或网络应用开发的人都可以参与，调查时间为2025年7月15日至8月15日，结果将于9月15日发布。所有数据将公开，供开发者和公司参考。

In 2023, after the State of JS and State of CSS surveys had already been going on for a few years, we realized something was missing: what about the technology that brings it all together?
After all, HTML now goes beyond tags and attributes, encompassing APIs for dynamic updates, rich embeds, performance hints, templating & components, and more.
The first State of HTML, led by web superstar
Lea Verou
broke all previous records for a new survey with 21,000 respondents, and introduced new UI paradigms that improved all future surveys.
This year, with Lea back at the helm, we added ✨35 new features✨, and introduced two new sections:
Graphics & Multimedia
and
Performance
.
What's more, survey results will be taken in consideration by browser vendors when deciding on their roadmaps, so participating can help shape the future of the web!
Are you ready? Get, set, go!
Loading...
FAQ
How long will answering the survey take?
Depending on how many questions you answer (all questions can be skipped), filling out the survey should take around 10-15 minutes.
Who should take this survey?
This is an open survey for anybody who makes websites or web apps, whether regularly or occasionally, as part of their job, as a student, or just for fun!
What are the survey's goals?
The survey's goals are to measure awareness of new HTML features and browser APIs, and help developers keep track of how their usage is evolving.
How will this data be used?
All data collected will be released openly for any developer or company to consult. Browser vendors also
use this data
to prioritize focus areas and inform their roadmaps.
When will the results be released?
The survey will run from July 15 to August 15, 2025, and the survey results will be released around September 15, 2025.
Who runs this survey?
This survey is run by
Devographics
together with a collective of contributors, translators, and volunteers.
How was this survey designed?
This survey was designed as the results of an
open design process
involving browser vendors and the web development community.

主要讨论点：Hoare的观点在其实践性和历史背景下的适用性

不同观点：
• FrankWilhoit部分认同Hoare的观点，认为Hoare的许多看法是正确的，但指出其中许多在Hoare所处时代的机器上是不切实际的，主要是由于资源不足。
• 有人认为即使后来资源不再成为限制因素，Hoare的原则也未被重新审视和应用，主要原因是这些原则的实施会要求对运行中的系统进行破坏性的更改。

补充讨论：
• Hoare的观点虽有前瞻性，但在其提出时缺乏实际操作性，导致在技术条件成熟后也未被广泛采纳。
• 讨论中提到技术和资源限制对理论和实践之间差距的影响，表明即使有价值的理论也可能因其实施成本过高而被搁置。
• 争议的焦点在于Hoare的原则是否应在资源充足的现代被重新评估和应用，以及实施这些原则是否仍然过于 disruptive（具有破坏性）。

data.title: Pockets Are a Significant, Untapped Market
data.author: vidyesh
data.article_summary: 这篇文章强调了市场对带口袋服装的强烈需求，尤其是女性服装。数据分析显示，每月有超过257,300次搜索涉及带口袋的服装，其中短裤类搜索量最高。具体关键词如“带口袋的跑步短裤”显示出高商业意图，表明消费者愿意为此功能付费。同时，搜索查询如“为什么女性裤子没有口袋”反映了用户的挫败感，突显出口袋是未被满足的核心需求。文章建议电商网站应添加口袋筛选功能，以改善用户体验并提高销售转化率。此外，男性短裤市场也存在类似需求，建议为男性带口袋短裤创建专门页面。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：女性服装缺乏口袋的原因及其背后的社会、历史和经济因素

不同观点：
• **时尚与美学优先**：设计师为了保持女性服装的“女性化”轮廓，避免加入口袋，担心口袋会影响服装的外观和线条。这种设计选择反映了时尚界对女性身材美学的传统标准和偏见。[1][3][5]

• **历史性别角色**：从17世纪开始，男性服装普遍有了口袋，而女性服装则往往没有。这是因为社会普遍认为女性不需要携带物品，特别是金钱和钥匙等，这些由男性负责管理。这种设计反映了历史上的性别不平等和性别角色分工。[2][4][5]

• **社会控制论**：有证据显示，在某些历史时期（如法国大革命期间），女性被禁止使用口袋，以限制她们携带或隐藏物品的能力，这反映了当时社会对女性独立性和流动性的控制意图。[5][6]

• **经济因素与配饰产业**：有人认为，限制女性服装口袋的设计是为了推动女性购买手袋和钱包，从而维持配饰市场的需求。一些品牌通过销售手袋获得的利润高于在服装中加入口袋的成本，这种商业策略已延续多年。[5]

• **成本节约**：加入功能性口袋可能会增加材料和生产时间，因此一些品牌选择使用较小或假口袋来节省成本。不过，这仅是问题的一部分，更深层次的原因与历史传统和社会观念有关。[5]

补充讨论：
• **传统的延续**：尽管在现代社会中女性的地位和角色发生了变化，但女性服装的口袋设计仍然落后于男性服装，许多专家认为这是过时的设计习惯和性别化的时尚思维的延续。[4][5]

争议焦点：
• **性别不平等的反映**：评论中对女性服装缺乏口袋的现象是否反映了深层次的性别歧视和社会对女性独立性的限制存在争议。部分观点认为现代时尚设计应更注重实用性和平等，而非延续历史上的性别偏见。[1][2][5][6]

• **时尚与功能的平衡**：时尚界在设计女性服装时，是否应更多考虑功能性（如增加实用口袋）而不是仅仅追求美学效果，这也是一个讨论的焦点。[3][5]

44733068.article_content:
What starts with a P and ends with an S that every single woman dreams about? POCKETS!
Real world pocket CTA in store!
We pulled data from Semrush to make this point: people want pockets!  It took us a few minutes to do this data-dive that reveals an enormous, untapped market. Across just four main clothing categories, there is a combined total of over
257,300 monthly searches
for items with pockets. This staggering volume confirms that pockets are not a minor detail but a primary, non-negotiable purchasing criterion for hundreds of thousands of shoppers.
Key Finding: Market Demand Exceeds a Quarter of a Million Monthly Searches
Pockets Breakdown by Clothing Category
Checking Semrush quickly, we can see that shorts, dresses, skirts and women's pants are sought with pockets. The demand is not evenly distributed. "Shorts" are the clear leader, accounting for over half of the total search volume. There’s a caveat: this specific query is gender-neutral. Men also want shorts with pockets. They want shorts with pockets with such an intensity that they represent almost 50% of the shorts category we looked at.
This is likely driven by athletic and lifestyle needs, as evidenced by top keywords. We have some running shorts, biking shorts, gym shorts, running shorts, you name it! Disclaimer: we did some back of the napkin data analysis. We’re not paid for this, we just want pockets! However, if you are curious like us (and want pockets), check out this table breaking down the top monthly searches for each category:
Clothing Category
Total Monthly Search Volume
Top Commercial Keywords
Shorts
143,800
biker shorts with pockets (1.9K), running shorts with phone pocket (1.9K), bike shorts with pockets (1.6K)
Dresses
75,300
dress with pockets (1.9K), dresses with pockets (1.9K), black dress with pockets (720)
Skirts
24,500
skirts with pockets (1.0K), skirt with pockets (720), maxi skirt with pockets (590)
Pants
13,700
women's cargo pants with pockets (590), women's pants with pockets (480), women's yoga pants with pockets (480)
The Strategic Implications of Pockets
The data reveals more than just volume; it exposes user intent, frustration, and a clear path to higher conversions if you help customers find clothing items with pockets.
High Commercial Intent
: Shoppers use specific, long-tail keywords like
running shorts with phone pocket
and
biker shorts with pockets
. This shows they are actively looking for a solution to a specific need and are ready to buy.
Active User Frustration
: Search queries for pants include questions like
why do women's pants not have pockets
. This is a direct signal from the market that a core need is being consistently ignored, creating an opportunity for any brand that listens.
DIY Intent Proves It's a "Must-Have"
: For dresses and skirts, users are searching for instructions on
how to add pockets to a dress
(260 monthly searches). When customers are willing to perform alterations themselves, it proves the feature is a necessity, not just a preference.
Clear SEO & UX Mandate
: This data provides an undeniable business case. Creating dedicated filters, categories, and landing pages for clothing "with pockets" is the most direct way to capture this high-intent traffic, improve the user experience, and increase sales.
We really, really, really want pockets. It bears repeating.
Build the "Pockets" Filter Now
Given the high search volume for women's clothing with pockets, particularly in categories like shorts and dresses, online clothing brands should implement a pocket filter in their women's section. This filter would cater to the substantial number of shoppers actively seeking garments with pockets, as evidenced by specific search terms like "running shorts with phone pocket" and "dress with pockets." Implementing such a filter would significantly improve user experience, streamline the shopping process for customers with this specific need, and likely increase conversion rates by directly addressing a key purchasing criterion.
We advise you to create landing pages or category pages for men’s shorts with pockets.

data.title: Examining mushrooms under microscopes helps engineers design stronger materials
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了通过研究蘑菇的微观结构来启发设计更坚固的材料。重点研究了白色纽扣蘑菇和舞茸这两种可食用蘑菇的菌丝网络。研究发现，菌丝（hyphae）的排列方式对其宏观强度有重要影响。白色纽扣蘑菇的菌丝较薄且交错排列，弹性约为18兆帕，类似于天然橡胶。而舞茸具有两种菌丝，其中较厚的骨骼菌丝平行排列，使其硬度达到560兆帕，接近高密度聚乙烯的硬度。计算机模型进一步证明，改变菌丝的角度可以调控材料的强度，而不需要改变其化学成分。这种研究有助于开发环保的强韧材料。

Pick up a button mushroom from the supermarket and it squishes easily between your fingers. Snap a woody bracket mushroom off a tree trunk and you’ll struggle to break it. Both extremes grow from the same microscopic building blocks:
hyphae – hair-thin tubes
made mostly of the
natural polymer chitin
, a tough compound also found in crab shells.
As those tubes branch and weave, they form a lightweight but surprisingly
strong network called mycelium
. Engineers are beginning to
investigate this network
for use in eco-friendly materials.
Filaments called hyphae are a mushroom’s support structures both above and below ground, and the mycelium network links multiple mushrooms together.
Milkwood.net/Flickr
,
CC BY-NC-SA
Yet even within a single mushroom family, the strength of a mycelium network can vary widely. Scientists have long suspected that how the hyphae are arranged – not just what they’re made of – holds the key to understanding, and ultimately controlling, their strength. But until recently, measurements that directly link microscopic arrangement to macroscopic strength have been scarce.
I’m a mechanical engineering Ph.D. student at Binghamton University who studies bio-inspired structures. In
our latest research
, my colleagues and I asked a simple question: Can we tune the strength of a mushroomlike material just by changing the angle of its filaments, without adding any tougher ingredients? The answer, it turns out, is yes.
2 edible species, many tiny tests
In our study, my team compared two familiar fungi. The first was the
white button mushroom
, whose tissue uses only thin filaments called generative filaments. The second was the
maitake, also called hen-of-the-woods
, whose tissue mixes in a second, thicker type of hyphae called skeletal filaments. These skeletal filaments are arranged roughly in parallel, like bundles of cables.
The two types of mushrooms used in the study: The white button mushroom is monomitic, shown on the left, meaning it has only one type of hyphae. The maitake is shown on the right, and is dimitic, meaning it has two types of hyphae.
Mohamed Khalil Elhachimi
After gently drying the caps and stems to remove any water, which can soften the material and skew the results, we zoomed in with scanning electron microscopes and tested the samples at two very different scales.
First,
we tested
macro-scale compression. A motor-driven piston slowly squashed each mushroom while sensors recorded how hard the sample pushed back – the same way you might squeeze a marshmallow, only with laboratory precision.
Then we pressed a diamond tip thinner than a human hair
into individual filaments
to measure their stiffness.
The white mushroom filaments behaved like rubber bands, averaging about 18 megapascals in stiffness – similar to natural rubber. The thicker skeletal filaments in maitake measured around 560 megapascals, more than 30 times stiffer and approaching the stiffness of high-density polyethylene – the rigid plastic used in cutting boards and some water pipes.
The two mushrooms tested include the maitake, left, and the button mushroom.
Lance Cheung/USDA and edenpictures/Flickr
,
CC BY
But chemistry is only half the story. When we squeezed entire chunks, the direction we squeezed in mattered even more for the maitake. Pressing in line with its parallel skeletal filaments made the block 30 times stiffer than pressing across the grain. By contrast, the tangled filaments in white mushrooms felt equally soft from every angle.
A digital mushroom and twisting the threads
To separate geometry from chemistry,
we converted
snapshots from the microscope into a computer model using a
3D Voronoi network
– a pattern that mimics the walls between bubbles in a foam. Think of ping-pong balls crammed in a box: Each ball is a cell, and the walls between cells become our simulated filaments.

data.title: Actions reflect your priorities
data.author: pbardea
data.article_summary: Tom Brady在周刊 newsletter 中分享了他对生活和成功的反思。他提到高尔夫球手Scottie Scheffler在赢得比赛后对庆祝的看法，引发了自己对个人满足感的思考。Brady回顾自己在27岁时也曾对职业成就作为满足感的标准感到怀疑，经过多年才明白，真正的满足感来自多个方面，而不仅是单一的成就。他以金字塔比喻生活的不同优先级，从自身健康、伴侣、孩子、工作、家庭到社区，每个阶段都有不同的优先事项。Brady强调，追求卓越的过程比结果更重要，生活中需要平衡多个角色的需求，以获得全面的满足感。

主要讨论点：药物高昂费用对个人选择的影响以及社交媒体内容呈现的合理性。

不同观点：
• rsyring认为，行动应反映个人的优先事项，但在面对高价药物时，个人选择被外部因素（如药物价格）所限制。他以自己孩子治疗嗜睡症的药物Xyrem为例，指出无论是否支付高额药费，都无法真正体现他的优先事项，而是反映了社会或其他人的优先事项对个体的影响。

• darod则没有直接回应药物费用问题，而是对社交媒体内容呈现表示不满，暗示对两个关于Tom Brady的帖子同时出现在首页感到不解和不满，可能认为这是对公众注意力的不合理引导。

补充讨论：
• rsyring提供了具体的例子（Xyrem药物的价格），使得讨论更加具体和现实，强调了在医疗费用高昂的情况下，个体选择如何被扭曲或限制。
• darod的评论引发了对社交媒体算法或内容推荐系统的质疑，暗示平台可能没有很好地反映用户的实际兴趣或优先事项。
• 争议的焦点可能在于，rsyring关注的是现实生活中的医疗决策困境，而darod则关注虚拟空间中的信息呈现问题，两者虽未直接交锋，但反映了不同层面的优先事项和关注点之间的冲突。

His answer was basically ‘not very long.’ For Scottie, celebrations have been fleeting, in part because golf doesn’t fulfill the “deepest desires of his heart.” The golf course, he said, is not where he goes to find satisfaction. So “what’s the point?” (That was the line that went most viral.)
When I heard this, some of it resonated with me, because I had a similar experience around his age. But I also understood that what I was hearing was a young athlete trying to make sense of success without the benefit of the perspective that comes with years of experience.
In this week’s newsletter, I want to give you some personal insight from my own experiences that I think will help explain where true personal satisfaction comes from—it comes from
many
places, not just one—and how you create it every day, win or lose, by the way you show up in each part of your life.
REFLECTION
In 2005,
I gave an interview to “60 Minutes”
where I sounded a little bit like Scottie Scheffler. I’d won three Super Bowls in my first four years as a starter, and I was explaining to the interviewer how, when I looked at my trophies and Super Bowl rings, I found myself thinking, “there’s gotta be more than this…this can’t be all…”
​
I was 27 years old. I was young. My first son, Jack, wouldn’t be born for another year-and-a-half. Football was a very important part of my life. But similar to Scottie, I could feel myself resisting the expectation placed on elite athletes, by the media and by society in general, to use professional achievement as the primary meter for personal satisfaction.
“What else is there for me?” I asked myself during that interview.
“What’s the answer?” the interviewer wondered.
“I wish I knew,” I said.
I would figure it out, but it took time. The lessons came in stages. First, that there is more to life than playing football and winning championships. Then I learned exactly what those other things were. Then, I learned how they all fit together so that what I did on the field supported the things I did off the field, and vice versa. And finally,
most importantly,
I learned that it was the pursuit of excellence in each of these areas where I found the most joy, not in the achievements themselves. It was the process, not the outcome.
I’m 25 years removed from the beginning of my pro football career, and a lot has changed since that interview. I have three kids now. I’ve played for two teams. I’ve started companies, invested in start-ups, taken ownership stakes in teams in multiple sports. I have teammates
and
employees now. I’m a broadcaster. I am a spokesperson, a business partner, a father, a friend and a brother and a son. I’m a decent golfer and a good leader. I have deep ties to both my local community and the global community.
Like most people, I have a lot going on. I don’t just do one thing. I do many things, though not all at the same time. I can’t. No one can—at least not if they want to be great at as many things as possible without sacrificing the satisfaction that can be derived from pursuing all the other things they care about.
LESSON
We all have different parts of our lives. You can think of them like a pyramid. At the top is yourself, and your physical, mental, and emotional health. Then there’s the relationship with your significant other or partner. Then you have your children, then your work, then your extended family, your friends, your hobbies, and finally your greater community.
​
Every layer of that pyramid is a priority. At any given moment, one of these priorities is taking precedence over the others. And the question is always whether it’s the right priority for the moment. That is the question it seems Scottie Scheffler is wrestling with: do I have my priorities straight? But I think figuring out that answer is fairly straightforward. When the priority is to take care of your mental and physical health, which is #1 always, that’s what you do. First you take care of yourself, then your partner, then your kids, and so on. When the priority is to take care of your career, whether it’s a three-week training camp or four rounds of major cham

data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：地铁系统的列车规模、车站设计及其运营效率

不同观点：
• **支持小列车和小车站的观点**：认为小列车和小车站可以降低建设成本，并且通过增加列车频次来弥补运力不足。这种方案在自动化操作下尤其有效，能够提高系统的灵活性。（例子：新加坡环线最初设计为小列车、小车站，以实现高频次运营）

• **质疑小列车和小车站的观点**：指出小列车在高峰期容易导致拥挤问题，且一旦系统运力达到上限，改造难度和成本极高。例如，新加坡环线因出乎预料的高客流，导致高峰期拥挤和长时间等待问题难以解决。（例子：新加坡环线高峰期拥堵）

• **关于等待时间和发车间隔的讨论**：认为地铁系统的等待时间是影响出行效率的重要因素，尤其是不确定的等待时间会增加出行的不便。即使系统频繁发车，若等待时间过长或不可预测，乘客体验仍会受到影响。（例子：即使在优秀公共交通系统中，等待时间仍是主要问题）

• **关于列车频次与速度的权衡**：提出列车频次增加可能会降低行驶速度，且存在安全最小车距限制，因此小列车高频次的方案可能在速度上有所妥协。（例子：慕尼黑地铁尝试通过压缩信号系统增加列车频次，但仍面临拥堵问题）

• **提出创新解决方案**：建议短列车但长站台设计，通过将站台划分为多个登车区，使得列车能够更紧密地调度，从而提高整体线路的通过能力。（例子：不同列车服务模式在同一线路上的交替停站方案）

补充讨论：
• **对现有系统的批评与比较**：有评论指出，类似的小型化方案在一些现有系统中并不新颖，例如Hudson Bergen轻轨。还有人提到自动化和长列车是长远减少运营成本的有效方式。

• **对实际操作性的担忧**：有人质疑小列车方案在非自动化系统中的安全性与可操作性，并提到维护成本和车站设计的复杂性。（例子：小列车可能增加维护需求和车站调度难度）

争议的焦点：
• **小列车与大运力之间的平衡**：一方面认为小列车和小车站能节省成本，另一方面指出高峰期拥挤问题和改造难度大，凸显出小列车方案在实际操作中面临的困境。

• **自动化与人力操作的取舍**：讨论中涉及自动化系统能提高小列车方案的可行性，但也有人担忧自动化对系统安全性和维护要求的挑战。

• **等待时间与乘客体验**：关于如何有效减少等待时间，提升乘客出行体验的讨论贯穿始终，尤其在高峰期和系统出现延误时，如何平衡发车间隔和运力是争议的另一个焦点。

data.author: akkartik
data.article_summary: 《Fantasy & Science Fiction》v004n06是1953年6月的科幻与奇幻杂志，属于英文的经典纸浆杂志系列。该期包含多种类型的科幻和奇幻故事，代表了1950年代早期的科幻文学。杂志大小为223.5M，由Internet Archive Python库1.0.10版本扫描上传。用户可以下载多种格式如EPUB、PDF、HOCR等，适合不同阅读需求。该杂志在2017年5月1日由The Pulp Librarian上传至网络存档，包含用户评论和较高的阅读量。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一篇包含"Bach beetle"概念的科幻故事的各种联想和延伸讨论

不同观点：
• [ggm] 认为 Bach beetle 的行动会有特定的模式，但这种模式是复杂的、看似无序的，甚至可能是分形的。这暗示了故事中可能包含的科学或数学元素。
• [Jtsummers] 提供了故事的直接链接，为其他讨论者提供了查阅原始文本的便利，但并未对故事内容发表具体看法。
• [Terr_] 提出了一种科幻设想，将歌曲《It's A Small World After All》的歌词嵌入耐辐射奇球菌的基因组中，并提供了一个相关研究的链接。这一观点扩展了故事中可能涉及的生物科技和数据存储的讨论。
• [zabzonk] 认为该作品并非 Philip K. Dick 的最佳作品，但指出该期杂志中有多位著名通俗文学作家，这可能是对该期杂志整体质量的评价。
• [stronglikedan] 建议故事中应使用鸟类，并提供了一个视频链接来支持其观点，可能是认为鸟类的行为或象征意义更适合故事的主题。
• [readthenotes1] 指出了故事《Ants》的作者与创造罗杰·摩尔饰演的圣人的角色之间的关系，这可能是对作者创作背景的补充。

补充讨论：
• [thimkerbell] 提到了对Hacker News用户去掉点击诱饵的额外加分，这似乎是在呼吁更真实和直接的讨论，可能暗示讨论中有标题党或误导性的信息。

总体来看，讨论围绕故事内容、科学设想、作者背景以及相关延伸材料展开，参与者从不同角度提供了联想和资源，丰富了对原故事的理解和讨论。

data.title: Emacs: The macOS Bug
data.author: xlii
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了Emacs在MacOS上的一个长期存在的性能问题，即随着使用时间的增加，Emacs的RAM占用不断上升，最终导致冻结。尽管在Linux和Windows上没有类似问题，作者发现MacOS上的Emacs在处理事件时会频繁分配和释放资源，尤其是在高DPI显示器下，这导致大量无用的缓存对象累积，从而影响性能。问题主要出现在`[NSApp run]`的调用上，它在处理系统事件时会无意中创建和销毁大量资源，如窗口、字体和图形上下文。由于MacOS高效处理事件的特性，这些问题在快速硬件上更加明显，最终导致Emacs无法正常释放资源，引发内存和CPU占用过高的问题。虽然问题复杂，但作者对代码设计并不持批评态度，而是理解其历史和维护难度。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Emacs在不同平台（尤其是macOS和Windows）上的性能问题及其技术实现的争议

不同观点：
• **Emacs在GUI框架中的主循环问题**：  
  - [rayiner] 指出Emacs希望控制主循环，而大多数GUI框架也有自己的主循环，这导致了兼容性问题。不过，他在Mac上的使用体验一直不错，特别是在处理多GB的PDF时表现良好。
  
• **macOS的严格性对Emacs的潜在改进**：  
  - [rahen] 认为macOS对Emacs中一些不够优雅的实现（如X11代码）的严格要求可能会促进跨平台的改进，比如采用更现代的SDL工具包，并且提到PGTK前端已经从macOS版本中获益。

• **对Emacs开发的兴趣与贡献问题**：  
  - [dwb] 表示对Emacs开发有兴趣，但缺乏时间和精力，只能表达感谢。

• **Windows平台的性能问题**：  
  - [vim-guru] 提到Emacs在macOS和Linux上表现良好，但在Windows上性能较差，甚至需要手动修补代码以完成编译。

• **macOS上Emacs内存管理问题**：  
  - [mattlangston] 分享了他在macOS上长期使用Emacs进行系统工程开发的良好体验，但也提到了打开大量缓冲区和长时间运行的内存使用情况。
  - [kkylin] 指出了Emacs在macOS上删除frame时内存未释放的问题，并提出了临时的解决方法。

• **Emacs在macOS上的性能不佳与用户困扰**：  
  - [eviks] 认为Emacs的性能问题在macOS上并不新鲜，早有用户提出，但未得到彻底解决。
  - [lygaret] 提到了macOS上线程睡眠可能导致LSP问题，并分享了一个个人补丁。
  - [algo_lover] 详细描述了在macOS上长期遭遇的性能和卡顿问题，并考虑转向其他编辑器，如NeoVim或Zed。

• **对Emacs与Cocoa框架的整合讨论**：  
  - [quotemstr] 建议让Emacs和Cocoa各自发挥优势，不必强行改变Emacs的核心设计，并提到使用w32-like独立线程的解决方案。

• **非自由操作系统上Emacs使用体验的争议**：  
  - [hollerith] 认为一些Emacs维护者可能故意让非自由操作系统上的使用体验不佳，暗示政治性原因。

• **内存分配器与构建问题的技术讨论**：  
  - [anthk] 建议使用Jemalloc解决内存问题，并讨论了Lucid构建在macOS上的可行性。

• **终端使用Emacs的偏好**：  
  - [jrockway] 偏好于在终端中使用Emacs，认为这样可以避免许多图形界面相关的问题，特别是在Linux和macOS上，并推荐了Kitty终端。

补充讨论：
- Emacs在macOS和Windows上的性能和内存管理问题是争议的焦点，尤其是macOS上的主循环冲突和内存泄漏。
- 用户对Emacs的长期卡顿和性能问题感到困扰，部分用户正在考虑转向其他编辑器。
- 一些技术解决方案和补丁被提出，但尚未被广泛采纳或整合进主线版本。

Emacs: The MacOS Bug
The Context
I have been recently roaming.
Doing some Zig, doing some Go, some Janet. Some C integration. Should have focused on my project but life threw more at me than I could handle, so I sought… happy distractions.
My experience with those technologies taught me new tricks and one day, when I needed some more distraction, I decided to debug something that had made me furious for years: Emacs jank
1
.
Whatever build I tried, whatever configuration I used, Emacs always rose in RAM usage. It became slower and slower within hours of use and eventually froze completely, requiring a kill.
I have read many complaints about performance searched for debugging techniques, possible causes etc. Some things helped others didn’t, but nothing made my experience closer to that on Linux or Windows.
All the sanctioned profiling I did hadn’t uncovered any anomalies. Crashdumps looked fine, sometimes showing that a hang happens on
ns_select_1
; something I wouldn’t expect to be a problem. Everything was reporting near-perfect behavior. Only thing that seemed off was CPU and MEM heavy
redisplay_internal
, but rendering big canvas on a HiDPI display might be costly.
Seemed to be “It’s not you, it’s me”. Until I got my hands on the traces.
Meta-consideration
Before going any further, I need to emphasize that, after spending more than a week digging into nsterm.m
2
, I’m not critical about the design or implementation
It’s easy to claim that something was badly designed or implemented inefficiently. Experience often points to simple reasons: growing complexity and lack of time.
In Emacs’ specific code case for MacOS, I could almost see how it developed over time and how layers upon layers were carefully layered, slowly tangling roots into a complex mesh. With the ever-changing MacOS API, maintaining the code likely took more effort than maintainers could provide. Besides,
it’s not a secret
that MacOS isn’t the primary platform - which explains the multiple flavors of Emacs on MacOS: Emacs Doom, MacPorts Emacs, Emacs Makefile, Homebrew distribution, Homebrew Emacs-Plus or Mitsuharu Yamamoto’s emacs-mac, to name a few.
Even though the bug exists on such a non-primary platform, the visible care of the code makes it easy to track. For me - and I’m not an expert in Objective-C, C or MacOS system engineering.
Issue
The problem is awkward as because it revolves around
[NSApp run]
3
invocations.
What this invocation does is it starts the main run loop, draining all pending event (the queue is shared) and then exits. It doesn’t seem to be problematic at all. Yet, it’s often used to process upcoming low-level system messages. Notably inside
ns_select
(replacement for
pselect
) and
ns_read_socket
, a communication pipe between “core” Emacs and GUI.
And inside it, there is barely visible side effect. Run invocation often occurs within
NSAutoreleasePool init
, which starts blank memory slate. Since it initiates a blank run, it creates everything that the main run loop would do during initialization: It creates windows, initializes graphical context, loads glyphs, fonts, and draws the frame.
It sounds horrible. But does it make sense? If it’s that bad - why didn’t anyone notice?
Because Emacs is very efficient.
This invocation is run as a response to an event - which can be almost anything. MacOS processes events rapidly in an async way. However, it’s also very efficient at juggling resources. Emacs, a pinnacle of engineering excellence, sets up and tears down resources in milliseconds.
…and the faster your hardware is, the faster it happens.
For instance, dragging a window handle - depending on the machine - could result in thousands if not millions of such events, causing allocation and reallocation of gigabytes of memory; Emacs is preparing you a new, laid-out window that is deallocated half a millisecond later because you’re not done yet.
Rapid allocations and deallocations cause various issues. Some allocations aren’t released. On purpose, because it’s the “core” Emacs which should handle closing, releasing resources, etc. However, if it didn’t expect those phantom instances, some small allocations might hang. NSMenu items, some strings, and glyphs could be affected. Emacs is unaware that
pselect
might be doing that, so it’s not cleaning them up.
Amusingly, when MacOS sees thousands of similar allocations, it starts to… cache them, “perceiving” them as important. They’re mostly useless: already loaded font glyphs in live windows, menu strings, copies of the current state of the rendered frame for use in the next re-rendering events. Those objects are allocated in hundreds of thousands, maybe millions. However, things like Emacs variables, search results reads, and counted in 100s are being pushed out further and further.
All of this processing is unbounded. The faster your Mac can process the events, the more loops happen. The higher DPI of your display - the bigger IOSurface size
4
and the bigger t
44737676.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了Emacs在MacOS上的一个长期存在的性能问题，即随着使用时间的增加，Emacs的RAM占用不断上升，最终导致冻结。尽管在Linux和Windows上没有类似问题，作者发现MacOS上的Emacs在处理事件时会频繁分配和释放资源，尤其是在高DPI显示器下，这导致大量无用的缓存对象累积，从而影响性能。问题主要出现在`[NSApp run]`的调用上，它在处理系统事件时会无意中创建和销毁大量资源，如窗口、字体和图形上下文。由于MacOS高效处理事件的特性，这些问题在快速硬件上更加明显，最终导致Emacs无法正常释放资源，引发内存和CPU占用过高的问题。虽然问题复杂，但作者对代码设计并不持批评态度，而是理解其历史和维护难度。

data.title: Traccar: an open source GPS tracking system
data.author: saikatsg
data.article_summary: Traccar是一个开源的GPS跟踪系统，包含基于Java的后端服务，支持超过200种GPS协议和2000多种GPS设备型号。它兼容主流SQL数据库，并提供REST API便于集成。Traccar解决方案包括网页应用、Android和iOS管理应用，以及用于跟踪移动设备的客户端应用。其功能包括实时GPS跟踪、驾驶行为监控、报告生成、地理围栏、报警通知、账户和设备管理，以及电子邮件和短信支持。项目遵循Apache-2.0许可证，由Anton Tananaev和Andrey Kunitsyn等人维护。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：自托管系统的功能和可配置性

不同观点：
• precommunicator认为该自托管系统运行良好，能够追踪所有设备，并且可以连接到车内硬连线的GPS设备。他还提到该系统支持几乎无限的GPS设备和协议列表，具有高度的可配置性。他通过在车内添加蓝牙温度信标，并编写特定计算属性，成功将原始温度数据转换并保存，展示了系统的灵活性。
• cranberryturkey则对precommunicator的描述表示需要更多具体例子，暗示对系统的实际应用和配置细节缺乏直观的理解。

补充讨论：
• precommunicator通过个人经验提供了具体的使用场景，如追踪设备和车载GPS集成，并详细描述了如何通过计算属性处理温度数据，展示了系统的强大功能。
• cranberryturkey的评论反映了部分用户可能需要更详细的操作示例以理解和使用该系统。这表明尽管系统功能强大，但其复杂性和配置需求可能对某些用户构成挑战。
• 争议的焦点在于系统的易用性和用户对具体实例的需求。虽然precommunicator展示了其个人成功案例，但cranberryturkey则代表了那些需要更明确指导的用户群体。

Traccar
Overview
Traccar is an open source GPS tracking system. This repository contains Java-based back-end service. It supports more than 200 GPS protocols and more than 2000 models of GPS tracking devices. Traccar can be used with any major SQL database system. It also provides easy to use
REST API
.
Other parts of Traccar solution include:
Traccar web app
Traccar Manager Android app
Traccar Manager iOS app
There is also a set of mobile apps that you can use for tracking mobile devices:
Traccar Client Android app
Traccar Client iOS app
Features
Some of the available features include:
Real-time GPS tracking
Driver behaviour monitoring
Detailed and summary reports
Geofencing functionality
Alarms and notifications
Account and device management
Email and SMS support

data.title: The hype is the product
data.author: lr0
data.article_summary: 文章指出，大型上市科技公司不再专注于客户需求，而是更关心股东和股票价格。决策者往往通过股票期权或与股票表现挂钩的奖金获利，导致产品只需“勉强够好”来留住用户即可。垄断成为硅谷的核心商业模式，不同服务商之间缺乏互操作性，如Google Workspace和Microsoft 365之间的文件共享困难，这是商业决策而非技术限制。这种壁垒使得用户即便不满服务，也不愿迁移到其他平台，从而被持续剥削。公司利用炒作维持高股价，如Meta从元宇宙转向AI的策略，尽管曾因元宇宙损失巨额资金。科技公司通过制造 hype 推动股票上涨，而非改善产品服务。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：科技公司是否因追逐短期利益和炒作而忽视客户体验，以及AI技术是否被过度炒作。

不同观点：
• johndhi认为，科技公司不一定需要垄断才能忽视客户体验，许多上市公司为了追求股价和投资者利益，会倾向于炒作而非专注于客户体验。同时，指出ChatGPT的成功在于其改善了搜索体验，表明长期忽视客户需求是错误策略。
• marcellus23反驳了反LLM（大型语言模型）的观点，认为这些工具并非毫无用处，虽然存在"幻觉"问题，但仍有部分文本生成与现实相关。批评将LLM视为无用的观点为卢德主义。
• ankit219对一项关于开发人员因使用AI工具而降低生产力的研究提出质疑，指出该研究存在多种限制条件，不能一概而论。
• mrweasel认为资本主义体系出现问题，导致产品质量下降但价格上升，并以特斯拉股票为例，说明其价格与公司实际表现无关，完全是炒作驱动。
• bagacrap将责任归咎于金融行业，认为科技公司只是对市场力量作出反应。以Meta为例，指出扎克伯格是在市场压力下才转向AI。
• pedalpete认为当前市场充满恐惧和贪婪，正处于炒作周期中，并引用市场杠杆趋势数据支持观点。
• micromacrofoot提出社会受"氛围"驱动，市场变得越来越不理性，谎言和负面情绪可以轻易影响市场价值。
• h2zizzle认为炒作是财富不平衡的产物，资本流入"愚蠢的婴儿潮事物"，并指出年轻人的意见因缺乏资本而被忽视，经济灾难可能是唯一能改变现状的途径。
• alsefj抱怨LinkedIn用AI替代传统工作搜索功能，导致用户体验下降，并决定删除账户。

44737346.article_content:
Large publicly traded tech companies seem to no longer consider their
customers – that is, people and organizations who actually buy their
products or pay for access to their services – their core focus. The
focus has instead turned towards the stock price.
Their real clients, the entities they
really
care about, are
the stockholders. Reasons are many, perhaps one of them being that
people making decisions tend to own stock options or have bonuses tied
to stock performance of the companies they run.
This means that for a large, established tech company the product or
service it offers does not matter all that much anymore. It needs to be
just barely good enough to keep people using it. The easiest way to do
this is some form of a monopoly.
Monopoly is the business model of Silicon Valley, and
they are not even shy
about that
.
Monopoly as a business model
¶
If you ever tried moving an organization wholesale from Google
Workspace to Microsoft 365 (or
whatever it is called this
week
), you know what I mean.
These are two sets of office productivity services; on a basic level
their functionality is very similar. Mail, calendar, contacts, document
editing, access controls, and so on. And yet you can’t even directly
share a file from Google Workspace to a person who uses Microsoft 365
(or vice-versa) in a way that would allow them to access it within their
own service, using their existing account, without manually exporting
and importing the file.
Sidenote
¶
This lack of basic interoperability is not a technical necessity but
a business decision. For example,
Open Cloud
Mesh
protocol allows for a lot of interoperability between providers
of such office productivity services, and is implemented by
Nextcloud
.
What this means in practice is that two people with accounts on
different independently-run instances of any software implementing this
protocol, hosted at two different providers, could not only share, but
collaborate on a file – each from their own account, using a familiar
interface.
Someone confidently using one of the two largest online office suites
can quite reasonably feel completely lost when presented with the
interface of the other. Interoperability and data portability between
them seems like science fiction, to a point where it is genuinely
difficult for some people to even understand the concept.
Barriers to migration
¶
What this means in practice is that it does not matter if people
using their services
hate
them
– it only matters that they don’t hate them
strongly
enough
to want to go through hell of migrating over to some other
(or
the
other) provider.
With a barrier to migration between providers this high, people using
the service can be exploited in all sorts of ways they could not have
been otherwise.
Cory
Doctorow aptly calls that enshittification
.
At the same time, though, this also makes it really difficult for
service providers to compete on quality of the service or its features.
It’s not enough to have a product that is just
a bit
better
than the competition. It has to be
so much better
that it makes
it worthwhile for people to go through the hell of migrating over.
That’s a tough sell – that’s kind of the point of creating these
barriers in the first place.
And yet the line must go up. Somehow, tech companies need to convince
investors that their services are really becoming
so much
better
– so that they keep paying more and more for company
stock.
Enter the hype.
Learning to ride the Gartner
cycle
¶
Hype, of course, is nothing new.
Gartner even
made a graph about it
, a long time ago.
Using hype to sell products barely anyone actually needs for prices
that make no sense has a long and storied history – so much so that
“tulip mania” has basically become a cliché. Using hype to scam people
out of their money outright (instead of selling them something tangible,
albeit at an unreasonably inflated price) is also not particularly
innovative. Just ask
Elizabeth
Holmes
.
What’s new here, I think, is large, established companies using hype
not to push products or services, but to push their stock. And doing so
in unison, pumping the same bubble together.
Big Tech paid close attention to the cryptocurrency and NFT bubble.
They
tried
to
get
in
on it
, but they mostly failed. Probably the most useful thing that
emerged from the whole NFT frenzy was that Twitter’s
erstwhile
hexagonal profile pictures
for NFT holders
made it trivial to block
cryptobros
for a time.
Then, Facebook tried to manufacture their own hype bubble with
Metaverse, somewhat piggy-backing on NFTs – and even changing the
company name (
partially to
distract from their culpability in Rohingya genocide
). Metaverse was
inevitable
.
Anyone not on the Metaverse
would
unavoidably be left behind
.
Mark Zuckerberg bet the shop on that particular hype.
The
shop lost 46.5 billion-with-a-b USD
on it. Zuckerberg
took
“full responsibility” by firing eleven thousand people
.
Today
Meta
is pivoting to – you guessed it – AI
.
Pivot to

data.author: upofadown
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了即将发生的网络崩溃风险，将其比作"request smuggling"问题的重生。具体而言，通过发送带有两个Content-Length头的HTTP请求，可导致代理和服务器解析不一致，引发混乱。作者担心自己的HTTP/1.1服务器是否会受影响，但他的Go语言编写的代理和服务器因统一的请求解析方式，可能避免此问题。作者的代理在读取请求时，通过`ReadRequest`读取并做出重要决策，然后通过`Request.Write`发送至后端，且如Content-Length等特殊头信息不来自常规头映射，确保请求一致性。文章还批评了某些代理（如Akamai）生成无效请求的问题，强调若代理生成错误请求是严重错误。最终，作者等待验证其代理是否会因该问题而失效。

44737823.article_content:
polarizing parsers
The web as we know it will soon crash and burn in a fiery death. 12 days. There’s even a
countdown
. This is apparently a redux of
request smuggling reborn
. Request research reborn redux.
I was a little concerned, because I’ve got some HTTP/1.1 servers here, and oh no, what should I do? To very briefly summarize the original research (which is very interesting, especially some of the techniques for detecting and exploiting the flaw), they send an HTTP request with two Content-Length headers, and then one proxy reads a certain amount while a backend server reads a different amount. Chaos and madness ensue.
Can this happen here? My proxy is written in go, as are most of my servers. So the good news is they will probably parse all the requests the same way, but even so, I believe the design of my proxy makes this attack impossible. It reads a request with
ReadRequest
, takes a look at some headers like Host and Url to make important decisions, and then writes it to the appropriate backend with
Request.Write
. Reviewing the source code, special headers like Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding don’t even come from the normal header map.
Whatever the proxy request parser decides the request is, that’s what it becomes and that’s what the backend sees. Portswigger also found a poorly implemented access control bypass using two Host headers, which shouldn’t be possible. What I want to emphasize is that there’s no requirement that go follow any particular standard correctly. It can use the first header or the last header, but once the request has been parsed, it’s fixed. The logic that looks at the host to determine where this request is going next looks at exactly the same string that later gets put into the host header. That’s the only header that will appear on the wire. The parser has effectively polarized the input, and now everyone will see it the same way. The polarizer may be installed the wrong way around, but even so, the output is always coherent.
So what is Akamai (it’s always Akamai) doing that their proxy is putting invalid requests on the wire? Why are we blaming the protocol here, when it’s clear (to me) that the error is the proxy that sends invalid requests? If you put crap on the wire, that’s bad. If your supposed web firewall is the one putting crap on the wire, that’s really bad. Yes, someone somewhere has to deal with the crap input, but why is anything in your stack generating crap? That’s just deranged.
Anyway, 12 days to go, spooky countdown, and then I found out if my proxy is irredeemably broken and needs to die, or if this is just Akamai screwing up again.

data.article_summary: Meka Agent 是一个开源的自主代理工具，通过视觉模拟人类操作进行高级网页浏览。它具有灵活的框架，支持自定义模型、工具和基础设施。目前在 WebArena 基准测试中达到72.7%的成绩。用户可通过 Meka App 免费试用并获得10美元信用额度。使用 Meka 需安装核心 SDK，配置 API 密钥，并选择合适的 AI 和基础设施提供商。示例代码展示了如何初始化代理并执行任务，如总结新闻文章。更多示例可在项目文件中查看。

Meka Agent
Meka Agent is an open-source, autonomous computer-using agent that delivers state-of-the-art browsing capabilities. The agent works and acts in the same way humans do, by purely using vision as its eyes and acting within a full computer context.
It is designed as a simple, extensible, and customizable framework, allowing flexibility in the choice of models, tools, and infrastructure providers.
Benchmarks
The agent primarily focuses on web browsing today, and achieves state-of-the-art benchmark results in the WebArena Benchmark (72.7%).
Read more
about the details of the benchmark results.
Meka App
If you would like to get started with browser automations without any setup, visit the
Meka App
to try the Meka Agent with $10 in free credits.
Getting Started
To get started with Meka, we packaged various providers that we have extensively tested. There are two main pieces:
A vision model that has
good visual grounding
. From our experimentation, OpenAI o3, Claude Sonnet 4, and Claude Opus 4 are the best US-based models. We have not experimented with Chinese-based models but would love to see contributions!
An infrastructure provider that exposes OS-level controls, not just a browser layer with Playwright screenshots. This is important for performance as a number of common web elements are rendered at the system level, invisible to the browser page. (Examples include dropdown menus, browser alerts, file uploads, and more)
To get started, we choose OpenAI o3 as the model and Anchor Browser as the VM-based infrastructure provider. We are open to submissions by other infra providers with OS-level controls!
Install the main components of the SDK
npm install @trymeka/core @trymeka/ai-provider-vercel @ai-sdk/openai @trymeka/computer-provider-anchor-browser playwright-core
Create your .env file and enter your API keys from the starter providers
OPENAI_API_KEY=GET FROM https://platform.openai.com/settings/organization/api-keys
ANCHOR_BROWSER_API_KEY=GET FROM https://app.anchorbrowser.io/api-access
Start the agent

Hierarchical Reasoning Model
Reasoning, the process of devising and executing complex goal-oriented action sequences, remains a critical challenge in AI.
Current large language models (LLMs) primarily employ Chain-of-Thought (CoT) techniques, which suffer from brittle task decomposition, extensive data requirements, and high latency. Inspired by the hierarchical and multi-timescale processing in the human brain, we propose the Hierarchical Reasoning Model (HRM), a novel recurrent architecture that attains significant computational depth while maintaining both training stability and efficiency.
HRM executes sequential reasoning tasks in a single forward pass without explicit supervision of the intermediate process, through two interdependent recurrent modules: a high-level module responsible for slow, abstract planning, and a low-level module handling rapid, detailed computations. With only 27 million parameters, HRM achieves exceptional performance on complex reasoning tasks using only 1000 training samples. The model operates without pre-training or CoT data, yet achieves nearly perfect performance on challenging tasks including complex Sudoku puzzles and optimal path finding in large mazes.
Furthermore, HRM outperforms much larger models with significantly longer context windows on the Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus (ARC), a key benchmark for measuring artificial general intelligence capabilities.
These results underscore HRM’s potential as a transformative advancement toward universal computation and general-purpose reasoning systems.
Quick Start Guide 🚀
Prerequisites ⚙️
Ensure PyTorch and CUDA are installed. The repo needs CUDA extensions to be built. If not present, run the following commands:
#
Install CUDA 12.6
CUDA_URL=https://developer.download.nvidia.com/compute/cuda/12.6.3/local_installers/cuda_12.6.3_560.35.05_linux.run
wget -q --show-progress --progress=bar:force:noscroll -O cuda_installer.run
$CUDA_URL
sudo sh cuda_installer.run --silent --toolkit --override
export
CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda-12.6
#
Install PyTorch with CUDA 12.6
PYTORCH_INDEX_URL=https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu126
pip3 install torch torchvision torchaudio --index-url
$PYTORCH_INDEX_URL
#
Additional packages for building extensions
pip3 install packaging ninja wheel setuptools setuptools-scm
Then install FlashAttention. For Hopper GPUs, install FlashAttention 3
git clone git@github.com:Dao-AILab/flash-attention.git
cd
flash-attention/hopper
python setup.py install
For Ampere or earlier GPUs, install FlashAttention 2
pip3 install flash-attn
Install Python Dependencies 🐍
pip install -r requirements.txt
W&B Integration 📈
This project uses
Weights & Biases
for experiment tracking and metric visualization. Ensure you're logged in:
wandb login
Run Experiments
Quick Demo: Sudoku Solver 💻🗲
Train a master-level Sudoku AI capable of solving extremely difficult puzzles on a modern laptop GPU. 🧩
#
Download and build Sudoku dataset
python dataset/build_sudoku_dataset.py --output-dir data/sudoku-extreme-1k-aug-1000  --subsample-size 1000 --num-aug 1000
#
Start training (single GPU, smaller batch size)
OMP_NUM_THREADS=8 python pretrain.py data_path=data/sudoku-extreme-1k-aug-1000 epochs=20000 eval_interval=2000 global_batch_size=384 lr=7e-5 puzzle_emb_lr=7e-5 weight_decay=1.0 puzzle_emb_weight_decay=1.0
Runtime: ~10 hours on a RTX 4070 laptop GPU
Trained Checkpoints 🚧
ARC-AGI-2
Sudoku 9x9 Extreme (1000 examples)
Maze 30x30 Hard (1000 examples)
To use the checkpoints, see Evaluation section below.
Full-scale Experiments 🔵
Experiments below assume an 8-GPU setup.
Dataset Preparation
#
Initialize submodules
git submodule update --init --recursive
#
ARC-1
python dataset/build_arc_dataset.py
#
ARC offical + ConceptARC, 960 examples
#
ARC-2
python dataset/build_arc_dataset.py --dataset-dirs dataset/raw-data/ARC-AGI-2/data --output-dir data/arc-2-aug-1000
#
ARC-2 official, 1120 examples
#
Sudoku-Extreme
python dataset/build_sudoku_dataset.py
#
Full version
python dataset/build_sudoku_dataset.py --output-dir data/sudoku-extreme-1k-aug-1000  --subsample-size 1000 --num-aug 10

data.title: Scammers unleash flood of online gaming sites
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary:
诈骗者利用Discord和其他社交媒体平台发布大量精美的在线游戏和赌博网站广告，通过提供免费积分吸引用户，最终盗取用户存入的加密货币。这些骗局通常冒用知名网红如Mr. Beast的名义，宣称与其有合作，并提供2500美元的积分奖励。用户需创建账户才能领取积分，玩精美的视频游戏，但当试图提现“奖金”时，网站要求进行“验证存款”，即存入约100美元的加密货币。然而，显示的“奖金”是虚假的，存款后资金再也无法取回。

这些骗局涉及超过1200个诈骗网站，使用相同的技术基础设施和API密钥，且通过独特的比特币钱包接收资金，阻止用户提现。受害者还可能受到自称“追款专家”的二次诈骗。骗子通过追踪IP地址和设备信息，防止用户在多个网站重复注册，显示这些网站由同一实体操控。

44738132.article_content:
Fraudsters are flooding Discord and other social media platforms with ads for hundreds of polished online gaming and wagering websites that lure people with free credits and eventually abscond with any cryptocurrency funds deposited by players. Here’s a closer look at the social engineering tactics and remarkable traits of this sprawling network of more than 1,200 scam sites.
The scam begins with deceptive ads posted on social media that claim the wagering sites are working in partnership with popular social media personalities, such as
Mr. Beast
, who recently launched a gaming business called
Beast Games
. The ads invariably state that by using a supplied “promo code,” interested players can claim a $2,500 credit on the advertised gaming website.
An ad posted to a Discord channel for a scam gambling website that the proprietors falsely claim was operating in collaboration with the Internet personality Mr. Beast. Image: Reddit.com.
The gaming sites all require users to create a free account to claim their $2,500 credit, which they can use to play any number of extremely polished video games that ask users to bet on each action. At the scam website gamblerbeast[.]com, for example, visitors can pick from dozens of games like
B-Ball Blitz
, in which you play a basketball pro who is taking shots from the free throw line against a single opponent, and you bet on your ability to sink each shot.
The financial part of this scam begins when users try to cash out any “winnings.” At that point, the gaming site will reject the request and prompt the user to make a “verification deposit” of cryptocurrency — typically around $100 — before any money can be distributed. Those who deposit cryptocurrency funds are soon asked for additional payments.
However, any “winnings” displayed by these gaming sites are a complete fantasy, and players who deposit cryptocurrency funds will never see that money again. Compounding the problem, victims likely will soon be peppered with come-ons from “recovery experts” who peddle dubious claims on social media networks about being able to retrieve funds lost to such scams.
KrebsOnSecurity first learned about this network of phony betting sites from a Discord user who asked to be identified only by their screen name: “
Thereallo
” is a 17-year-old developer who operates multiple Discord servers and said they began digging deeper after users started complaining of being inundated with misleading spam messages promoting the sites.
“We were being spammed relentlessly by these scam posts from compromised or purchased [Discord] accounts,” Thereallo said. “I got frustrated with just banning and deleting, so I started to investigate the infrastructure behind the scam messages. This is not a one-off site, it’s a scalable criminal enterprise with a clear playbook, technical fingerprints, and financial infrastructure.”
After comparing the code on the gaming sites promoted via spam messages, Thereallo found they all invoked the same API key for an online chatbot that appears to be in limited use or else is custom-made. Indeed, a scan for that API key at the threat hunting platform
Silent Push
reveals at least 1,270 recently-registered and active domains whose names all invoke some type of gaming or wagering theme.
The “verification deposit” stage of the scam requires the user to deposit cryptocurrency in order to withdraw their “winnings.”
Thereallo said the operators of this scam empire appear to generate a unique Bitcoin wallet for each gaming domain they deploy.
“This is a decoy wallet,” Thereallo explained. “Once the victim deposits funds, they are never able to withdraw any money. Any attempts to contact the ‘Live Support’ are handled by a combination of AI and human operators who eventually block the user. The chat system is self-hosted, making it difficult to report to third-party service providers.”
Thereallo discovered another feature common to all of these scam gambling sites [hereafter referred to simply as “scambling” sites]: If you register at one of them and then very quickly try to register at a sister property of theirs from the same Internet address and device, the registration request is denied at the second site.
“I registered on one site, then hopped to another to register again,” Thereallo said. Instead, the second site returned an error stating that a new account couldn’t be created for another 10 minutes.
The scam gaming site spinora dot cc shares the same chatbot API as more than 1,200 similar fake gaming sites.
“They’re tracking my VPN IP across their entire network,” Thereallo explained. “My password manager also proved it. It tried to use my dummy email on a site I had never visited, and the site told me the account already existed. So it’s definitely one entity running a single platform with 1,200+ different domain names as front-ends. This explains how their support works, a central pool of agents handling all the sites. 诈骗者利用Discord和其他社交媒体平台发布大量精美的在线游戏和赌博网站广告，通过提供免费积分吸引用户，最终盗取用户存入的加密货币。这些骗局通常冒用知名网红如Mr. Beast的名义，宣称与其有合作，并提供2500美元的积分奖励。用户需创建账户才能领取积分，玩精美的视频游戏，但当试图提现“奖金”时，网站要求进行“验证存款”，即存入约100美元的加密货币。然而，显示的“奖金”是虚假的，存款后资金再也无法取回。

data.author: rectang
data.article_summary: Ho Sau-Mei是香港仅存的几位麻将雕刻师之一，从事这一行已有四十多年。她从13岁开始跟父亲学习手艺，如今视力和体力大不如前，但仍坚持在红磡的小店里手工雕刻麻将牌。她的店铺狭窄简陋，工作台是一块玻璃展示柜。尽管麻将制作已大多被中国内地工厂取代，她仍使用传统工具，以精湛技艺雕刻、上色，完成一套手工麻将需10到14天，售价245美元。香港政府在2014年将麻将雕刻列入“非物质文化遗产”，但如今香港仅剩寥寥几位匠人，而她是唯一一位仍在工作的女性。尽管年近古稀，她继续工作以避免无聊，但承认体力大不如前。

The game is almost over for one of Hong Kongâs last mahjong carvers
Story by Kathleen Magramo, CNN
Photographs and video by Noemi Cassanelli, CNN
Published July 27, 2025
Ho Sau-Mei, one of Hong Kongâs last mahjong tile carvers, is getting old. âMy eyesight is fading, and my hands are getting sore,â she says brusquely as she chisels the intricate strokes of a Chinese character or the petals of a flower onto a piece of plastic little bigger than a postage stamp.
For over four decades, Ho has been carving mahjong tiles in a tiny roadside shop in Hung Hom, an old harborside district that is now seeing the rapid construction of shiny, new residential high-rises.
She started learning the craft at age 13 from her father, who founded the family's tile business, Kam Fat Mahjong, in 1962. Masters who would visit Hong Kong during its manufacturing heyday in the 1970s and 80s also shared their techniques and trained apprentices.
Ho Sau-Mei carves mahjong tiles at her shop in Hong Kong.
Mahjong is a game for four people similar to rummy and is hugely popular across China and among Chinese communities for which it also serves as a cultural ritual and symbol of tradition. Children learn how to play as they spend time with cousins and friends over Lunar New Year, and among the elderly itâs popular all year round.
Mahjong tiles are traditionally made of wood, ivory or bamboo, with tile makers cutting, polishing, carving and coloring each piece.
In the 1960s, there were more than 20 mahjong tile carvers in Hong Kong â and even an association dedicated to the industry.
Now most mahjong tiles are mass-produced in factories in mainland China.
Mahjong tiles are stacked on a game table in Hong Kong.
The craft was listed as an âintangible cultural heritageâ by the Hong Kong government in 2014, which provides funding for research into and preservation of various protected traditions.
But less than a handful of mahjong artisans are still around the city, and among them Ho is the only woman left practicing the craft.
A craft of precision
Minibuses and double-decker buses zoom past the busy road across her dimly lit ground-floor shop beneath a staircase on Bulkeley Street.
The store is barely two meters wide with a grimy glass case on the wall that reaches the ceiling filled with faded photographs and stacks of novelty mahjong tiles. Hovering behind Hoâs work stool is a shrine that glows a gentle red hue.
Ho starts to carve mahjong tiles in the morning.
Pictures of Ho can be found inside her shop.
Workers from nearby hardware stores and elderly people sheâs befriended over the years also banter with her. Pedestrians sometimes slow down to observe Ho deep in work hunched over her small working space.
Hoâs routine has stayed the same even as the neighborhood developed, with mahjong tiles now mostly made by big factories in mainland China.
Sheâs usually already seated at the storefront and lays out her tools for the day just before 10 a.m.
At 68 years old, Ho says she only works until about noon these days, sighing that she âdoesnât have the staminaâ to carve away all day anymore. She could retire if she wanted to, she says, âbut Iâll get bored.â
She lays out the Bakelite tiles lined neatly on a heavy wooden tray and prepares her specialized tools on the tiny glass display case that serves as her work desk.
Tiles are packaged inside Hoâs shop in Hong Kong.
Ho uses a traditional tool to carve a tile.
A complete mahjong set comes with 144 tiles, including the four suits â bamboo, dots, characters, directional winds (north, south, east and west) â and special tiles depicting flowers, dragons and the four seasons.
One of Hoâs tools resembles a giant corkscrew and is used to drill the concentric circles on one of the rectangles.
Using other tools with varying tips and angles, she holds the blank tiles with her calloused thumb and middle finger and masterfully etches the complicated Chinese characters and flower tiles with surgical precision.
Ho paints mahjong tiles inside her store.
For the penultimate process, Ho brings out vintage jars of paint, their labels weathered by time. âDonât go away, this part is fast,â Ho tells us.
She brushes red, green and blue colors onto the naked tiles, carefully bringing the engraved symbols to life.
A full set costs $245 and takes around 10 to 14 days to make by hand. But if youâre planning to order a set from Ho, the entire process is still analogue â and somewhat haphazard.
The phone rings a few times during the day with a handful of customers inquiring about the orders theyâve placed.  But Ho doesnât really keep track of the orders.
A client speaks with Ho and her assistant.
Mahjong tiles are seen in front of a small house temple at Hoâs shop.
Thereâs no online booking system. Everything is done either by phone or in person, and she scribbles the orders down on a notebook thatâs torn apart at the spine.

data.title: A Dive into Open Chat Protocols
data.author: Bogdanp
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了网站管理员使用Anubis系统来保护服务器免受AI公司大规模抓取数据导致的过载影响。Anubis采用了一种类似于Hashcash的“工作量证明”机制，在个人用户访问时几乎不增加负担，但在面对大规模抓取时则会显著增加成本。这一方案是一个临时解决办法，旨在为更复杂的身份验证技术争取时间。同时，文章提醒用户Anubis需要现代JavaScript功能，因此需禁用如JShelter等可能阻止这些功能的插件。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开放聊天协议及其使用中的问题

不同观点：
• PaulHoule认为，为了展示对AI爬虫的反对而故意让观众等待，是一种做作且让用户体验变差的行为。他明确反对通过让用户不便来表达立场，尤其提到了大科技公司通常采用这种让人不满的方式。
• 尽管PaulHoule批评了故意让用户不便的做法，但他同时指出，开放聊天协议是去"去垃圾化"（de-enshittification）难题中非常有趣且关键的一部分。他认可开放协议的技术潜力，并认为它们在技术社区中具有实际价值。

补充讨论：
• PaulHoule提到了XMPP协议，尽管它被认为"不够酷"，但在特定领域（如军队和警察）中非常流行。他给出的例子包括将XMPP定制用于存储与公众互动的信息，或者用于战地报告。这表明某些技术在特定专业环境中具有实用性，尽管在大众文化中并不受欢迎。
• 争议的焦点在于如何在不损害用户体验的前提下表达对某些技术（如AI爬虫）的反对，以及开放协议在广泛应用中的实际表现和认知差距。

44738216.article_content:
Making sure you're not a bot!
Loading...
Why am I seeing this?
You are seeing this because the administrator of this website has set up
Anubis
to protect the server against the scourge of
AI companies aggressively scraping websites
. This can and does cause downtime for the websites, which makes their resources inaccessible for everyone.
Anubis is a compromise. Anubis uses a
Proof-of-Work
scheme in the vein of
Hashcash
, a proposed proof-of-work scheme for reducing email spam. The idea is that at individual scales the additional load is ignorable, but at mass scraper levels it adds up and makes scraping much more expensive.
Ultimately, this is a hack whose real purpose is to give a "good enough" placeholder solution so that more time can be spent on fingerprinting and identifying headless browsers (EG: via how they do font rendering) so that the challenge proof of work page doesn't need to be presented to users that are much more likely to be legitimate.
Please note that Anubis requires the use of modern JavaScript features that plugins like
JShelter
will disable. Please disable JShelter or other such plugins for this domain.

• 另一位用户在Linux上构建时遇到需要多个API密钥的问题，对本地优先的软件需要这么多API密钥感到意外（polyaniline）。

44738323.article_content:
Tesla
Tesla Model S
Tesla stops taking Model S/X orders in Europe
Fred Lambert
| Jul 30 2025 - 8:10 am PT
64 Comments
Tesla has stopped taking new orders for its flagship Model S and Model X vehicles in Europe. It’s not the first time it happened, but it still raises questions.
Following the 2021 Model S/X refresh, Tesla ceased taking new orders for the vehicles in Europe for an unexpectedly long period.
The refreshed models were unveiled in January 2021, and Tesla continued to take orders through December 2021, after which they stopped.
It didn’t
reopen orders in Europe until August 2022
.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Now, something similar is happening with the new refresh.
In June,
Tesla unveiled another minor refresh of the Model S and Model X
.
Now, just over a month later, Tesla has stopped taking new orders for the Model S and Model X in Europe. The automaker deactivated the online configurators and instead, it redirects to the main Model S and Model X pages, where buyers can still find some inventory vehicles.
At this time, the reason for the stoppage in taking orders is unclear, but it may be due to a supply issue.
Tesla only produces Model S and Model X vehicles at its Fremont factory in California. With the last refresh, Tesla had difficulties ramping up production.
Now, Tesla has significantly reduced its production capacity for these vehicle programs, as
demand has declined over the last few years
.
Currently, Tesla quotes a 2-month wait time to receive a new, made-to-order Model S in California.
Electrek’s Take
Top comment by
Philip234
Liked by 13 people
According to Electrive, "The German Federal Motor Transport Authority (KBA) recorded just 58 new Model S and 59 new Model X registrations in the first half of the year..." If the EU's biggest market is only buying 10 of each model a month, it is probably no longer worthwhile to go through the homologation expense.
View all comments
When the lead time for ordering is too long, as it currently could be in Europe, and California is at 2 months, Tesla has sometimes shut down new orders.
It could be as simple as that.
Tesla needs to ramp up Model S/X production after the refresh to meet demand in North America before returning to Europe.
The automaker could also be careful about locking in a price for Model S/X months in advance. The US is now imposing 15% tariffs on Japan, where Model S/X battery cells are produced. The situation has been fluid, making it hard for Tesla to predict costs.

• [jmye] 则认为，很多人抱怨所有工作场所都是“toxic”，实际上可能是个人问题。如果一个人认为所有工作环境都有问题，那么可能是个人选择导致他们处于边缘地位。

data.author: mhutson

By
Matthew Hutson
